response.sql: WITH player_avg AS (SELECT bp.player_id, p.bats, AVG(bp."double") AS avg_doubles FROM batting_postseason bp JOIN player p ON p.player_id = bp.player_id GROUP BY bp.player_id, p.bats HAVING AVG(bp."double") IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_doubles) AS overall_avg FROM player_avg), indexed AS (SELECT pa.player_id, pa.bats, pa.avg_doubles, pa.avg_doubles / o.overall_avg AS idx FROM player_avg pa CROSS JOIN overall o), hand_avg AS (SELECT bats, AVG(idx) AS hand_idx FROM indexed GROUP BY bats) SELECT i.player_id, i.bats AS batting_hand, i.avg_doubles, i.idx AS index_value, i.idx - h.hand_idx AS index_minus_hand_avg FROM indexed i JOIN hand_avg h ON h.bats = i.bats WHERE i.bats IS NOT NULL ORDER BY index_minus_hand_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A player's average postseason doubles is the mean of the non-NULL `double` values across all of that player's batting_postseason rows, pooled over all years and rounds.

The overall average is the unweighted mean of the per-player averages, and it includes players whose batting hand is NULL. Players whose doubles are all NULL have no per-player average and are excluded from every average.

Each hand average is the mean of the index values of all players sharing that `bats` value, including the empty-string group. The final list is filtered to non-NULL hands only after these averages are computed.
Ties in index_minus_hand_avg are broken arbitrarily, since the request does not specify a secondary sort key. The query uses NULLS LAST, which requires SQLite 3.30+ or PostgreSQL.
